nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong tropical sun drives plant growth, though in the dry season much of the forest drops its leaves.

nodes.name: Seasonal rainfall
nodes.desc: A wet season from about October to April brings most of the water. Baobab trunks swell and shrink with it, and the long dry season leaves the forest mostly leafless.

nodes.name: Poor, dry soils
nodes.desc: Thin soils over limestone and sand in the west and south, with low and erratic winter rain, favour drought-adapted plants.

nodes.name: Soil decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and dead animals and return nutrients to the thin soil.

nodes.name: Grandidier's baobab
nodes.desc: Giant water-storing tree of seasonal dry forest. Its flowers open at dusk and are pollinated by hawk moths and nocturnal lemurs.

nodes.name: Tamarind
nodes.desc: A leafy tree whose pods are a key dry-season food for ring-tailed lemurs.

nodes.name: Spiny forest plants
nodes.desc: Woody, spiny, drought-adapted plants of the south-west that are only distantly related to cacti.

nodes.name: River algae and plants
nodes.desc: Algae and water plants growing in the rivers and wetlands that cross the dry forest.

nodes.name: Hawk moths
nodes.desc: Night-flying moths that carry baobab pollen from tree to tree while feeding on nectar.

nodes.name: Madagascan flying fox
nodes.desc: A large fruit bat that roosts in groups and feeds at night on fruit and flowers.

nodes.name: Ring-tailed lemur
nodes.desc: Opportunistic omnivore eating mainly fruit and leaves. Tamarind can make up a big share of its diet in the dry season.

nodes.name: Verreaux's sifaka
nodes.desc: Mostly a leaf eater, also taking fruit, flowers and bark. Infants are hunted by fossas and harrier-hawks.

nodes.name: Giant jumping rat
nodes.desc: A rabbit-sized burrowing rodent of western dry forest that eats plant material from the forest floor.

nodes.name: Radiated tortoise
nodes.desc: Grazing tortoise of the southern spiny thickets that feeds on plants.

nodes.name: Freshwater fish
nodes.desc: Fish of the seasonal rivers and lakes that graze on algae and small aquatic life.

nodes.name: Tenrecs
nodes.desc: Small insect-eating mammals unique to Madagascar, hunted by the fossa.

nodes.name: Chameleons
nodes.desc: Slow-moving lizards that catch insects with a sticky tongue and are eaten by lemurs, raptors and the fossa.

nodes.name: Madagascar ground boa
nodes.desc: A ground-dwelling constrictor that preys on ring-tailed lemurs and other small animals.

nodes.name: Madagascar harrier-hawk
nodes.desc: Raptor that kills some sifaka infants and also takes lemurs and reptiles.

nodes.name: Madagascar fish eagle
nodes.desc: Critically endangered eagle of western wetlands and lakes that hunts fish.

nodes.name: Fossa
nodes.desc: Madagascar's largest land predator. Lemurs make up over half of its diet, plus tenrecs, lizards, birds and rodents.

nodes.name: Nile crocodile
nodes.desc: Apex predator of western rivers and lakes that eats fish.
